Full Program · October 18–19, 2026

Conference
Schedule.

Two full days at Riverbend Learning Center. Day one puts you outdoors — field sessions, practicum workshops, and hands-on learning along the river. Day two brings everyone together for keynotes, peer roundtables, and honest conversation.

Rain or Shine Field sessions run outdoors Lunches included both days
Track Key:
Outdoor Field Track
Classroom Workshop Track
Professional Development Track

Full Conference Schedule

Day One · Friday, October 18, 2026
Workshops & Field Sessions
Field-based learning · Practicum workshops · Peer exchange
8:00 am 30 min
Registration & Morning Coffee
Riverbend Main Hall · Lobby

Check in, collect your field workbook and lanyard. Coffee, tea, and locally baked goods from Cultura Bakery in Asheville.

8:30 am 30 min
Welcome & Opening Circle
Outdoor Amphitheater

Opening remarks from the organizing team, land acknowledgment, and a quick orientation to the site and the two days ahead. Rain location: Main Hall.

9:00 am 2 hrs
Workshop Block A — Choose Your Track

A1 · South Meadow: Trail Interpretation in a Shifting Phenology Calendar — led by Maya Torres. Hands-on practice reading plant and animal indicators in the field. Limit 25.

A2 · Conference Room B: Risk Assessment Practicum — led by Ben Okafor. Walk through a dynamic risk matrix, role-play field scenarios with youth, and leave with a template you can customize. Limit 30.

A3 · Conference Room A: Funding Your Programs: Grant Strategies for Outdoor Education — led by Petra Novak. Covers federal, state, and private sources, common mistakes, and writing for non-specialists. Limit 30.

11:00 am 30 min
Trail Walk & Snack Break
River Loop Trail

Unstructured walking time along the Swannanoa River loop. Good for transition, decompression, and spontaneous peer conversation.

11:30 am 90 min
Field Session Block B — Outdoor Practicum

B1 · River Loop Trail: Inclusive Trail Design Walk — led by Lila Chen. Evaluate a real trail segment for access barriers. Teams rotate through assessment stations. Rain does not cancel this session.

B2 · Pine Ridge Area: Climate Indicators in the Field — led by Jordan Whitehorse. Read the land through Indigenous ecological knowledge and current phenological data side by side. Limit 20.

B3 · Outdoor Classroom: Youth Facilitation Lab — co-facilitated. Practice facilitation techniques with peer volunteers playing the role of youth participants. Feedback rounds included. Limit 18.

1:00 pm 60 min
Lunch — Locally Sourced
Riverbend Pavilion

Catered by Asheville Provisions. Menu includes vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options. Please indicate dietary needs during registration. Eat outside if the weather agrees.

2:00 pm 2 hrs
Workshop Block C — Afternoon Deep Dives

C1 · Conference Room A: Lesson Planning for Changing Conditions — Building curriculum that holds up when weather, seasons, and species ranges shift. Participants leave with a revised lesson template.

C2 · Conference Room B: Parent & Community Communication — How to explain risk, weather decisions, and outdoor learning to families who didn't grow up outside. Practical scripts and Q&A frames.

C3 · Main Hall — South: Certification & Professional Development Panel — What credentials matter, which are worth the investment, and how your organization can support staff growth. Q&A format.

4:00 pm 60 min
Unstructured Field Time & Sponsor Demo Area
Pavilion + Grounds

Explore sponsor tables, demo gear, wander the grounds, or grab a quiet corner for notes. No agenda.

5:00 pm 2 hrs
Evening Reception & Gear Swap
Riverbend Pavilion

Light bites, local beer and cider, and a community gear swap table. Bring gear you no longer need; take what you can use. First come, first served, no cost.

Day Two · Saturday, October 19, 2026
Talks, Roundtables & Demos
Keynotes · Peer roundtables · Sponsor demo hour
8:30 am 30 min
Morning Coffee & Networking
Main Hall · Lobby

Coffee, tea, and pastries. Open seating — a good time to find the people you wanted to meet yesterday.

9:00 am 60 min
Opening Keynote: Reading the Land
Maya Torres Main Hall Keynote

Integrating Climate Signals into Trail Interpretation. Maya opens the day with a full keynote on how the land speaks differently now — and how to help people hear it. Expect practical frameworks, not just inspiration.

10:00 am 50 min
Risk-Aware, Not Risk-Averse
Ben Okafor Main Hall

Dynamic Safety Planning for Youth Groups. Ben makes the case that the biggest danger in youth outdoor education isn't weather or terrain — it's programs so afraid of liability that they stop taking kids outside altogether.

11:00 am 50 min
No One Left on the Trailhead
Lila Chen Main Hall

Building Truly Inclusive Outdoor Classrooms. Lila shares research and program models that show inclusion doesn't require lowering the bar — it requires redesigning who sets it.

12:00 pm 90 min
Lunch & Peer Roundtables
Pavilion + Breakout Rooms

Facilitated roundtable topics include: climate communication for families, budgeting for outdoor programs, building trails in tribal territories, and neurodivergent youth in outdoor settings. Join any table, move if you want.

1:30 pm 50 min
Place-Based Learning Rooted in Indigenous Land Stewardship
Jordan Whitehorse Main Hall

Jordan, Land Relations Coordinator with the Eastern Band Cherokee Nation, discusses how place-based curriculum that ignores whose land it is produces educators with roots in midair — and how to ground the work differently.

2:30 pm 50 min
The Dose Makes the Medicine
Dr. Sam Adeyemi Main Hall

Nature Exposure, Mental Health, and Youth Outcomes. Dr. Adeyemi synthesizes 10 years of environmental psychology research into practical guidance: how much time outside, what kinds of activities, and what outcomes you can honestly claim.

3:30 pm 30 min
Sponsor Demo Hour
Pavilion

Sponsors demo gear, software, curriculum tools, and field equipment. Short format: 5–7 minutes each. Attendees move freely between demo stations.

4:00 pm 60 min
Closing Circle & Peer Exchange
Outdoor Amphitheater · Rain: Main Hall

Open mic format — share what you're taking home, what you're still wrestling with, and what you're going to try first. Facilitated by the organizing team. Bring a notebook.

5:00 pm
Conference Concludes · Safe travels

Rain & Weather Policy

Field sessions on Day One run rain or shine — dress accordingly (see our gear list). Indoor alternatives are available only for severe weather warnings issued by the National Weather Service. Keynotes and talks on Day Two are held indoors. October in Asheville averages highs in the low 60s°F — bring layers.

Ready to join us in October?

Early bird tickets are $180 and available until September 1, 2026.
